title: Ignition Coil Primary/Secondary Circuit
shortDescription: DTC P0350: ignition coil primary/secondary circuit fault.
fullDescription: DTC P0350 indicates Ignition Coil Primary/Secondary Circuit. Codes in the P0350-P036x range cover ignition coil primary/secondary circuits per cylinder. A misfire-related coil fault should be addressed before catalyst damage occurs.
safetyImpact: Active misfires can destroy the catalytic converter and cause stalling. A flashing check engine light means stop driving as soon as safe.

causes.cause: Water intrusion in spark plug well

symptoms: Smell of unburnt fuel / catalyst overheat

fixSteps.title: Confirm Cylinder
fixSteps.instruction: Read DTCs and misfire counters; identify which cylinder the coil code points to.

fixSteps.title: Swap-Test the Coil
fixSteps.instruction: Move the suspect coil to a known-good cylinder. If the misfire follows, the coil is bad.

fixSteps.title: Inspect Plugs and Boots
fixSteps.instruction: Pull the spark plug; check gap, condition, and signs of oil or coolant. Replace boot if cracked.

fixSteps.title: Test Coil Driver Circuit
fixSteps.instruction: Back-probe the coil control wire; verify trigger pulse with a scope or LED tester.

faq.q: Can I drive with an ignition coil code?
faq.a: Short distances only. A flashing CEL means active misfire that can destroy the catalytic converter within minutes.

faq.q: Should I replace all coils together?
faq.a: Not required, but if the engine is high-mileage and the coils are original, replacing the set saves labor.

faq.q: Is this a DIY repair?
faq.a: Yes on most engines. Coils on plug-tube engines are bolt-on with basic tools.
